summary: Skamania County, WA lookout site: an L-4 cab built in 1934, staffed into 1965 and burned in 1971; a gravel forest road now ends at the site.

facts.status_note: The cab was burned in 1971. No source I read describes remains on the ground at the site today.

access.note: Drive-up on Forest Road 31, which Willhite describes as good gravel to the site.

visit.trail_note: The road ends at the site, which is not the highest point. A very small road leads on to the true summit.

events.note: L-4 cab built about a quarter mile north of the summit at the end of the main road
A benchmark was placed, per Willhite
Announced as one of six lookouts to stay manned, mainly for communications coverage
Announced as the only manned lookout in the Spirit Lake and Lewis River districts
Forest Service burned the lookout house as no longer needed; the register says destroyed
Registered July 16, 2012 as US 1336, WA 236; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com say destroyed in 1971; Willhite and Forest Lookouts say the Forest Service burned the lookout house in 1971. Both describe the same end in the same year; the story says burned and notes the register's word.

notes_for_editor: Elevation conflict, not resolved and not in the story: the register and FireLookout.com give 3,434 ft (the record's 1,046.7 m), while Willhite gives 3,484 ft; Willhite gives the true summit as 3,515 ft. The 1964 and 1965 staffing comes from a Longview Daily News report as quoted on Forest Lookouts; the newspaper itself was not read, so the story attributes it to the quotation. The 'public' access level rests on the gravel Forest Road 31 and Willhite's drive-up note, with 2020 photographs; an editor should check current Forest Service road status. Willhite's timber-sale remark is speculation by him and is marked as such. The record is consistent with the sources (gone, ground, federal). Used 2 WebSearch calls and 4 page reads.
